thread:
jess: Heads-up — starting bring-up for amaris-9b (checkpoint from research group). License attached in the artifact bucket, asking for quick compliance triage and whether we can serve hosted embeddings.

jess: key ask: commercial hosting OK? quantized redistribution allowed? attribution text required? we ran a quick eval and saw a small QA regression after 4-bit quant.

mohan: pinging infra + legal. I started a quant run (GPTQ-4) on a node, results so far: 0.6% EM drop on our SQuAD-like bench, but a handful of hallucination regressions in multi-step prompts.

pat: can you paste the license or link? hard to triage blind.

jess: link: s3://redwood-models/amaris-9b/license.txt (copied relevant bits below)

jess: ```
Model License v1.2
- Permitted: commercial use, hosting, inference
- Redistribution: allowed for source weights if redistributed with original license and provenance file
- Quantized weights: derivative clause applies (sec 3.2) — "transformations that change numeric representation are derivatives"
- Attribution: UI-level credit required when model output is used in product (sec 4)
```

alex: ok license looks permissive but sec 3.2 catches quantization — means we may need to include the original provenance and keep the same license when distributing quantized weights.

sylvie: @jess thanks for the note. Quick Q: the attribution in sec 4 — is it a short string or a more prominent credit? can you paste the exact wording?

jess: the clause: "Include the text \"Model: Amaris-9B (Amaris Research)\" in close proximity to model-driven features, or in an about/legal page if UI constraints exist."

pat: that wording seems implementable in Console and SDK docs. For hosted API, we can add an attribution header in the response metadata too.

license-bot: automated check: provenance file present, license matches known template v1.2, patent-pool flagged? None detected. Recommend manual legal review for derivative/quantization specifics.

mohan: technical follow-up: if quantized weights are considered "derivative", do we need to open-source the quantized weights under the same license when using them internally for Dedicated/Private deployments? or is redistribution only triggered when we distribute outside Redwood (e.g., to customer pods or downloads)?

sylvie: good question. Short answer: redistribution obligations trigger when you provide the derivative to a third party or make it publicly available. Internal hosting under a service we operate typically doesn't count as distribution, but Dedicated (customer-reserved pools) where we hand over binaries to customer's infra could trigger redistribution.

sylvie: action: need to confirm whether Dedicated customers get binaries or just container images that we control. If we hand over raw quantized weight files, we should treat as redistribution and require provenance + license bundle.

alex: infra note — our Dedicated onboarding currently pushes OCI images that contain weights as tar in /opt/model by default for performance. That is effectively handing files to customer infra. Can change to a download-on-demand that streams weights from our control plane to avoid redistribution.

pat: legal/ops asks: if we keep weights in images, we need an automated packaging step to include provenance + license and a small README with required attribution text and a checksum file. Also add a flag in the Console UI to surface the attribution string.

jess: about embeddings: license doesn't forbid storing embeddings, but sec 6 has a clause about "derivation of datasets" — not clear. Any red flags about storing customer prompts/embeddings?

sylvie: storing customer data separate question: privacy/data-processing agreements and our existing TOS cover embeddings. From license POV, embeddings produced by inference are generally allowed to be stored, but if the license has a clause limiting "derivative datasets" we should avoid releasing a public embedding corpus derived from the model without attribution + provenance. For customer data, standard retention + DP policies apply.

mohan: on the quality side, do we need to hold off on hosted GA until we validate quantized model stability? The regressive hallucination cases are reproducible on a few prompts.

jess: recommended rollout: start internal canary on Dedicated staging, gate hosted public by passing regression thresholds (EM drop <1%, hallucination count <=2/1k prompts). We can expose a special header X-Model-Attribution in responses for tracing.

pat: ops will add packaging and attribution step. sylvie, can Legal confirm we can expose attribution header as that satisfies "close proximity" requirement?

sylvie: yes header + UI about page is acceptable for web apps. For mobile SDKs we may need in-app about text. We'll note that in the compliance checklist.

ci-bot: build pipeline started: quant-package job queued (job id: qpkg-8421). Logs will be under builds/qpkg-8421.

mohan: plan for next 48h: finish full eval sweep (qa, summarization, safety prompts) and add regression tests. If regressions persist after QAT (calibration) we'll try alternative quant strategy (bitsandbytes 8/4 hybrid).

jess: sylvie — I'd like sign-off for hosted embeddings & canary tomorrow if legal ok with redistribution caveats and attribution plan. Can you confirm by EOD?

sylvie: I'll review the provenance and the Dedicated packaging implications now. If we commit to keeping an image-based approach that hands customer files, we need Customer Distribution Addendum included. If we switch to streaming weights for Dedicated, that's fine. I should have a short note by EOD.

jess: thanks — will update the PR and add checklist items. :thumbsup:

pat: tagging ops playbook step: add packaging task + UI attribution flag + dedicated-streaming option.

mohan: leaving logs here for folks who want to repro:

mohan: ```
# reproduce quant artifacts
python quantize.py --input s3://.../amaris-9b/weights --method gptq --bits 4 --out ./amaris-9b-q4
# run eval harness
python eval_harness.py --model ./amaris-9b-q4 --bench squadsim --runs 1000
```

jess: cool — will follow up once CI finishes.

sylvie: +1, thanks everyone. I'll post the legal note here once I finish.
